indicators.note: to stifle something is to smother it, so one word is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: keeps, as in holds or possesses
a sharp smarting pain

explanation.surface: A soldier holds back the pain of a wound during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle' at the end could be a verb, but it names the famous fight of 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Hastings in 1066 is the famous clash where William the Conqueror defeated King Harold.

blocks.note: first meaning: the Trojan prince and champion killed by Achilles
second meaning: a verb, to intimidate or browbeat

explanation.surface: A thuggish warrior from Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector led the defence of Troy in the Iliad; to hector someone is to browbeat them, a verb sense.

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the next word

blocks.note: the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a degree
stale, as in no longer fresh

explanation.surface: A single man working at a long-established company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun; it is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady and secure, not likely to give way, like a solid footing.

clue.text: Little devil has skill to pass on

blocks.note: an imp is a small demon
has is a joining word; art is skill

explanation.surface: A mischievous child has a talent worth passing on.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart knowledge is to communicate or convey it to someone else.

clue.text: Means of transport showing first-class pedigree

blocks.note: first-class means very good
a strain is a line of descent or breed

explanation.surface: A thoroughbred horse with a fine pedigree, used for travel.
explanation.walkthrough: The break moves: GOOD STRAIN becomes GOODS TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A goods train is a British term for a freight train carrying cargo rather than passengers.

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: one who bows, as a courtier does before the throne
a sovereign is a gold pound coin, and L is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a royal attendant about the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: B(L)OWER. A sovereign is an old British gold coin worth one pound; L (from Latin libra) is the pound sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Blower is old British slang for a telephone, as in 'get on the blower'.

blocks.note: lo, an old word meaning look or see
the indefinite article
a thing is an affair or romance, as in having a thing with someone

explanation.surface: Someone watches a love affair unfold and is appalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing is intense dislike or revulsion, a noun matching disgust.

clue.text: It can be fatal in battle that's goin' on

blocks.note: battle, as in combat
faring, going on, with the dropped g shown by the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Deadly things happen in an ongoing battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfarin is an anticoagulant used as rat poison, and too much is fatal to humans as well.

clue.text: Took a break and made an impression

blocks.note: first meaning: adjourned, as a court or parliament does
second meaning: set back into a surface, like an alcove in a wall

explanation.surface: Someone paused for a rest and made a strong impact.
explanation.definitionFit: A body recesses when it adjourns; a recessed panel is indented, pressed into a surface.

indicators.note: something storing an item keeps it inside, so the plant holds the element

blocks.note: a wild flower with pink or white blooms
the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Something holds up a plant that stores gas, like a garden stake.
explanation.walkthrough: C(H)AMPION: the H goes in after the first letter of the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to advocate and back it publicly, a verb sense matching support.

clue.text: Material found in the analysis of a brick

indicators.note: analysis breaks words down, and the result is found within the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A lab examines a brick to discover what it is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth or textile, and also the physical stuff a building is made of.

indicators.note: rendered means made into something else, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some dental extraction left the patient's lips sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extractor' and 'rendered' suggest a dentist or melted fat; one is the definition, the other the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil press squeezes oil out of olives or seeds, so it is a machine for extracting.

definitions.note: shears is plural in form but names a single tool

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for son
picks up, as a radio receives a signal

explanation.surface: A boy lifts a tool from the shed floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picks up' looks like lifting the tool; it means catching a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Shears are large scissors used for cutting hedges or fleeces, a common garden implement.

clue.text: Selfish man about to withdraw money

indicators.note: about means around, so the man's name goes round what follows

blocks.note: a man's name
to go is to withdraw or leave
a cent is a coin

explanation.surface: A self-centred man is about to take money out of the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraw money' reads as a trip to the cash machine, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Egocentric means thinking only of oneself, self-centred, a close synonym of selfish.

clue.text: Giant fell floundering into the sea from boat

indicators.note: a giant that has fallen and is floundering is in disarray, so its letters get jumbled
into signals the jumbled word being put inside another

blocks.note: the letters of giant rearranged
brine is salt water, a poetic word for the sea

explanation.surface: A giant topples off a boat and flounders in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: BRI(GANTI)NE: the jumbled giant goes inside the salt water.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel, a type of ship.

clue.text: Spill the beans about select sport

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
to cull is to pick out or select

explanation.surface: An informer reveals secrets about a chosen sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculling is rowing with two oars per rower, a water sport raced at regattas.

clue.text: Shy maiden in court? I don't know

indicators.note: in places the first words inside the last

blocks.note: arch means coy or knowingly playful
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
a see is a bishop's seat, and the Holy See is the papal court

explanation.surface: A bashful young woman in a courtroom pleads ignorance.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as two words, an idiom said with a shrug; 'court' is a bishop's or pope's seat, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Search me is a casual idiom meaning I have no idea, inviting the asker to look for themselves.

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A design is submitted as previously planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Assigned can mean allotted or nominated, and put forward fits as proposed or designated for a task.

indicators.note: baffled means confused, so these letters are muddled

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Latin American revolutionary
the letters of species rearranged

explanation.surface: A revolutionary new species has left a man bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person here: chess pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece in chess, draughts and similar games is traditionally called a man.

blocks.note: William Penn, the Quaker who founded Pennsylvania
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Quaker settler depicted on a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow pointed banner flown from a lance or a ship's mast.

blocks.note: biking, cycling about, with the dropped g shown by the apostrophe
on joins the pieces; I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Getting about on a tropical island or coral reef.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands was the US nuclear test site that gave the swimsuit its name.

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the father's word wraps round the next

blocks.note: DA is a child's word for father, plus the S of the possessive
all, as in the whole lot

explanation.surface: Dad holds on to everything he owns in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: D(ALL)AS. The definition is only a place, which the solver locates as somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a large city in Texas, so it is somewhere found in the United States.

blocks.note: first meaning: Philip, the English poet who wrote 'The Whitsun Weddings'
second meaning: larking about, with the dropped g shown by the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A poet fooling around and playing a practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in playin' tells you to drop the final G as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was a major twentieth-century English poet; larkin' is lark-ing, fooling about.

clue.text: A nice gal prepared cake decoration

indicators.note: prepared, as food is made ready, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pleasant young woman has made a decoration for a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied green stalks of the angelica plant are a traditional garnish on cakes and trifles.

clue.text: Craving but lacking time for divination

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: itching to do something is craving it
the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone craving to know the future but short of time for fortune-telling.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the T from itching to get I CHING.
explanation.definitionFit: The I Ching is the ancient Chinese Book of Changes, consulted for fortune-telling by casting coins or stalks.

blocks.note: the abbreviation for president
managed, as in ran a business
a dial is a control knob

explanation.surface: A president took charge of running a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Prandial is the adjective from Latin prandium, a meal, so it means relating to dinner.

indicators.note: something that seizes another holds it tight, so the queen goes around the journalist

blocks.note: Lady Jane Grey, the nine-day queen of England in 1553
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A greedy English queen grabs hold of a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: GRE(ED)Y. 'English queen' tempts ER, but it is the surname of Lady Jane.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping describes someone avid for money or possessions, a synonym of avaricious or covetous.

blocks.note: to check is to scan or examine
ties, as in things that bind or fasten

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the straps on a piece of lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanties are skimpy knickers for women, a jokey British word for brief underpants.
